title: Legion real-PC test plan
evidenceRoot: %USERPROFILE%\legion-pc-run\<yyyymmdd>\ (outside the repo; never commit evidence that contains a token, key or .legion data)

areas.name: Installer
areas.rollback: Run uninstall.cmd (no /purge) in every test install folder; delete throwaway source copies, the foreign test folder and the fake Electron project; restore %USERPROFILE%\.legion from the G0 backup; undo any PATH or network change; stop any test node process by PID.

areas.name: Core and app shell
areas.rollback: Quit Legion from the tray; stop the port listener by PID; delete LEGION_HOME copies and test agents; restore %USERPROFILE%\.legion from the G0 backup; re-enable the network adapter; reset the Doctor-breaking change (re-enter the boat.dev key).

areas.name: Chat, Rooms and Library
areas.rollback: Delete test rooms, test agents and test Library notes (Inbox reject or Undo); remove exported vault folders; restore the data backup if settings were changed.

areas.name: MCP
areas.rollback: Run `claude mcp remove legion`; restore ~/.claude.json from the backup made in MCP-05; remove the redact-test server and any Claude Desktop config entry; untick MCP inheritance if you ticked it; delete the throwaway project folder.

areas.name: VM and boat.dev
areas.rollback: Stop every VM from the Computer card and confirm in the boat.dev dashboard that nothing is running; restore Settings, boat.dev, API base URL and remove the cost-estimate rates; stop the logging listener.

areas.name: Blender (local, live, VM, managed, extension)
areas.rollback: Delete the test task folders under %APPDATA%\legion\blender\local\ and the test exports; set the bridge back to its previous state; remove the community add-on or extension and any managed Blender copy only if installed for this run; kill test processes by PID only; stop VM Blender runs and the VM.

areas.name: BSV testnet wallet in a VM
areas.rollback: Freeze, Disarm and Disconnect in the BSV panel; delete the testnet VM and its wallet; nothing is ever configured on the host; a broadcast testnet transaction cannot be undone and has no value.

areas.name: BSV mainnet real funds
areas.rollback: R11: Disable mainnet, Disarm, Disconnect. Keep the audit log. A sent transaction cannot be undone; read the wallet history before anything else after any abort.

areas.name: Website and public install
areas.rollback: Uninstall the test install (uninstall.cmd); no other state changes.

areas.name: Perf and regression
areas.rollback: Delete scratch output folders and temp homes the scripts created; restore any power-plan change.

gates.name: Pre-flight
gates.rule: Owner confirms: which PC, Windows version, the build under test (commit), that nothing below runs against the owner's own funded wallet, and where evidence goes. Back up %USERPROFILE%\.legion and ~/.claude.json first.

gates.name: Installer
gates.rule: Run first. Everything else needs an installed build. INST-10 must pass before G2.

gates.name: Core and app shell
gates.rule: Needs a launching app (INST-10). Nothing in G3 to G11 starts until APP-01 to APP-03 pass or the owner accepts the failure in writing.

gates.name: Chat, Rooms, Library, MCP
gates.rule: Needs the owner's Claude sign-in (account class). Uses a little of the owner's Claude quota.

gates.name: VM and boat.dev
gates.rule: spends-money: needs the owner's explicit go and the boat.dev key. Stop the VM at the end of every check.

gates.name: Blender local and live (no downloads)
gates.rule: Needs a real Blender already installed. No downloads: checks with class downloads wait for G6.

gates.name: Downloads
gates.rule: Only with the owner's explicit go, one download at a time. Covers add-on pin, extension install, managed Blender, npm ci.

gates.name: Blender in the VM
gates.rule: spends-money and downloads inside the VM: owner go, boat.dev key.

gates.name: BSV testnet VM
gates.rule: real-wallet class: only inside the throwaway testnet VM, owner present at the keyboard, an agent never drives it. Never the owner's own wallet.

gates.name: Perf and regression
gates.rule: On an idle PC, after G2. Can run any time after that; do not run while other checks are in progress.

gates.name: Website and public install
gates.rule: Only after the product repo is public and the site is deployed.

gates.name: BSV mainnet real funds
gates.rule: LAST. real-funds class: owner present, says go, does every step by hand with the wallet's own UI. Needs BSVT-00 to BSVT-23 recorded and the independent review signed off.

checks.title: Double-click setup.cmd: window stays open on success and on a forced failure
checks.preconditions: Windows 10 or 11 with Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe, not pwsh). Unpacked source folder. Node installed for the success run. A second run with Node hidden from PATH (open a cmd window, run `set PATH=C:\Windows\System32` first) or with `npm ci` made to fail (disconnect the network) for the failure run.
steps: Success run: double-click setup.cmd in Explorer. Answer the prompts.
Failure run: from a cmd window with the reduced PATH, run setup.cmd, or double-click it with the network off after Node is found.
Note whether the window stays open at the end of each run and whether the message can be read.
checks.expected: On success the window stays open with a "done" style message (setup.cmd pauses). On failure it stays open with an error that names what failed. Neither run closes the window before it can be read.
checks.evidence: PC-INST-01-success.png, PC-INST-01-failure.png (window text visible); copy of the console text to PC-INST-01.log.

checks.title: Double-click setup-yes.cmd: closes on success, stays open with a message on failure
checks.preconditions: As INST-01. setup-yes.cmd is the unattended entry point (-Yes).
steps: Double-click setup-yes.cmd with everything in order and watch the window.
Repeat with Node hidden from PATH or the network off so a step fails (double-click, not from an open cmd window).
checks.expected: Success: the window closes by itself and Legion starts. Failure: the window stays open, prints "Legion setup failed (exit code N)" and waits for a key (the single `pause` after the redirect test).
checks.evidence: PC-INST-02-failure.png showing the failure message and the pause prompt; PC-INST-02.log.

checks.title: Redirected input: setup never waits for a keypress
checks.preconditions: cmd window in the source folder. A way to run with no console (Task Scheduler one-shot task) is optional.
steps: Run `setup.cmd < nul`.
Run `echo | setup.cmd`.
Run `cmd /c setup-yes.cmd -DryRun -NoLaunch` from a cmd window with output piped to a file.
Optional: create a Task Scheduler task running `cmd /c setup-yes.cmd -DryRun -NoLaunch` and run it.
checks.expected: None of the runs blocks on Read-Host or `pause`; each ends by itself. [Console]::IsInputRedirected gives the same answer in every case (no run waits).
checks.evidence: PC-INST-03.log with the exit code of each run and the wall-clock time.

checks.title: Process matcher stops only Legion processes
checks.preconditions: A build installed and running (INST-10). Four extra programs started first: (a) Legion running from the install folder, (b) a Legion source checkout on another drive with its own electron.exe running, (c) an unrelated Electron app whose folder has src\electron\main.ts and package.json with another name, (d) VS Code and a plain `node` dev server open. Use harmless sample apps only.
steps: List the candidate PIDs with `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.Name -match "electron|node" } | Select ProcessId,Name,CommandLine`.
Run `setup.cmd -DryRun` and read which PIDs it says it would stop.
Run `setup-yes.cmd -NoLaunch` and compare the list of surviving PIDs.
checks.expected: Only Legion's own PIDs (install folder and the source checkout of Legion, both with package name legion) are listed and stopped. The unrelated Electron app, VS Code and the node dev server keep running.
checks.evidence: PC-INST-04-before.txt and PC-INST-04-after.txt (PID lists), PC-INST-04.log (setup output).

checks.title: Install to a path with spaces and non-ASCII characters
checks.preconditions: Windows PowerShell 5.1. A folder such as C:\Users\Zoë Ørsted\Legion Test (create it, or use a user account with such a name).
steps: Run `setup-yes.cmd -InstallDir "C:\Users\Zoë Ørsted\Legion Test" -NoLaunch` from a source folder that also has a space in its path.
Open the Desktop and Start-menu shortcuts and start Legion from each.

checks.title: Dangerous -InstallDir values are refused (drive root, foreign folder, user profile)

steps: Run `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\setup.ps1 -DryRun -Yes -NoLaunch -InstallDir <target>` for each target: `C:\`, `C:`, the foreign folder, `%USERPROFILE%`, `%USERPROFILE%\.legion`.
Check the foreign folder afterwards.
checks.expected: Every target exits non-zero with a refusal and prints the resolved path. Nothing is deleted (keep.txt still there). A missing folder, an empty folder or an existing Legion install is accepted.
checks.evidence: PC-INST-06.log (exit code per target), listing of the foreign folder after.

checks.title: Uninstall: shortcuts, install folder and data folder behave as documented

Check Desktop (including the OneDrive Desktop), Start menu, the install folder and %USERPROFILE%\.legion.
Reinstall, then run `uninstall.cmd /purge` and answer the confirmation.
checks.expected: Shortcuts that point at this install go; the shortcut that points at another install stays. Install folder is removed. %USERPROFILE%\.legion is intact without /purge and deleted (after you confirm) with /purge.

checks.title: CRLF line endings survive ZIP download and git clone
checks.preconditions: Git for Windows with `core.autocrlf=input`. The repo (or a ZIP of it) once it is reachable for the owner.
steps: Download the repo ZIP and unpack it; run `Format-Hex -Path setup.cmd -Count 400` or check with `(Get-Content -Raw setup.cmd) -match "\r\n"`.
Run `git -c core.autocrlf=input clone <repo> clone-test` and check setup.cmd, setup-yes.cmd, uninstall templates and scripts\*.ps1 the same way.
Double-click setup.cmd from each copy.
checks.expected: All .cmd and .ps1 files have CRLF in the working tree in both cases (the index stores LF, .gitattributes converts) and run without "is not recognized" line-ending errors.

checks.title: SmartScreen and antivirus behaviour on the unsigned .cmd files
checks.preconditions: Default Windows Security and SmartScreen settings. File arrives via browser download (Mark of the Web) and also via git clone.
steps: Download the ZIP in a browser, unpack, double-click setup.cmd.
Note every prompt: SmartScreen, Defender, any third-party AV.
checks.expected: RECORD ONLY: which prompts appear and whether "Run anyway" lets setup finish. README already says to expect prompts. Anything that deletes or quarantines a file is a FAIL for the owner to triage.

checks.title: Fresh npm ci and build on Windows, launch from the shortcut with the real Electron binary

When it finishes, start Legion from the Desktop shortcut. Then close it and start `start-legion.cmd` in the install folder.
Open Doctor (title bar chip or type /doctor).
checks.expected: npm ci, build and the Electron download finish; the window opens; Doctor lists Node, config, Claude sign-in, boat.dev and workspace. Both launchers open the same app.

checks.title: Setup run from inside a Legion agent does not kill its own ancestor

steps: In the app, ask the agent to run `setup-yes.cmd -DryRun -NoLaunch` from a source folder and then (second run) `setup-yes.cmd -NoLaunch`.
Watch whether the app window and the core stay up and whether the run finishes.
checks.expected: Setup excludes the whole ancestor chain: the Legion process that launched it keeps running and the update completes. If the ancestor is stopped, that is a FAIL (review F6).
checks.evidence: PC-INST-11.log (PID list before and after), PC-INST-11.png.

Set LEGION_HOME to a throwaway folder and run `uninstall.cmd /purge -DryRun`; read the target.
Delete scripts\lib\legion-procs.ps1 from a copied install and run uninstall.cmd.

checks.title: Real Windows PowerShell 5.1: parse the scripts and run the matcher helpers on a throwaway node.exe
source: review/release-packaging-review.md F5, section 0 (5.1 never run in the review)
checks.preconditions: powershell.exe 5.1 (`$PSVersionTable.PSVersion` shows 5.x). Note: the repo CI job "installer (Windows PowerShell 5.1)" covers part of this on a GitHub runner, which is not the owner's PC.
steps: Run `powershell -NoProfile -Command "[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('scripts\setup.ps1',[ref]$null,[ref]$e) | Out-Null; $e.Count"` for setup.ps1, uninstall.ps1 and scripts\lib\legion-procs.ps1.
